newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans seen focus of 1997 bull spreading.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans seen focus of 1997 bull spreading.

text.p: Monday's U.S. Agriculture Department grain stocks report and planting intentions outlook fortified analysts' expectations for additional gains in nearby old crop contracts over the new crop months, especially in the soybean pit.
"I was optimistic the (July/November soy) spread would go to $2.00 to $2.20 (premium July) and today's report should help that along," said Dean Witter analyst Jerry Gidel.
The July/November soybean spread Monday closed at $1.65, premium July, which was 21 cents wider than the closing spread Thursday.
But there was not a noticeable hike in bull spreading Monday.

"I think a lot of people have been bull spreading all along," said Mark Cermak of Chicago-based trade house O'Connor and Co, referring to the lack of bull spreading numbers and players showing up on the CBOT player's sheets.
USDA Monday shocked market watchers by releasing a U.S. soybean planting outlook for 1997 of 68.8 million acres.
The figure was well above 64.21 million acres planted to soybeans in 1996 and also exceeded an average of analysts' expectations for 65.85 million acres.
Chicago Board of Trade November soybean futures tumbled on word of the estimates but nearby months held firm as USDA again reminded the market of relatively low soybean stocks in the U.S.
USDA said the supplies of U.S. soybeans as of March 1 totaled 1.078 billion bushels, below an average of analysts' expectations at 1.093 billion bushels.
"We're looking at phenomenal export sales and a great crush," said Andy Daniels, executive vice president of LFG Futures.
Traders and analysts also cited potential increases in the spread between CBOT July and December corn.
"Corn stocks suggest feeding rates were higher than expected and near-term corn prices should remain fairly firm," said Terry Francl, senior economist for the American Farm Bureau Federation.
USDA said March 1 U.S. corn stocks totaled 4.494 billion bushels, above trade expectations for 4.565 billion.
Bull spreaders enjoyed the stocks data and the government's outlook for corn seedings this year at 81.416 million acres, above expectations for 80.92 million, traders noted..
Smith Barney Monday was a key bull spreader of five million bushels of July/December, floor sources said.

The CBOT July/December spread Monday closed at 18-3/4 cents per bushel premium July, a 6-1/2 cent gain from Thursday's close. But some analysts said the momentum of that bull spread was likely to wane when the spread reaches the low twenty-cent-per-bushel area premium the July.
"I'm not wildly excited about more spread (spread widening) in the July/Dec. At the low 20's of that spread I would be a little cautious," Gidel said.
